title: Quiz: Crude Oil and Fractional Distillation

options.text: A compound of carbon and oxygen
A pure substance containing only one type of molecule
A complex mixture of hydrocarbons formed from the remains of ancient organisms

questions.explanation: Crude oil is a complex mixture of many different hydrocarbons (mainly alkanes) formed over millions of years from the remains of ancient marine organisms under high pressure and temperature.

questions.stem: How does fractional distillation separate crude oil into fractions?

options.text: By separating hydrocarbons based on their different boiling points
By reacting the oil with acids

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation works by heating crude oil and separating the hydrocarbons based on their different boiling points. Smaller molecules with lower boiling points rise higher up the column.

questions.stem: In a fractionating column, where are the fractions with the smallest molecules collected?

options.text: At the bottom of the column
At the top of the column
In the middle of the column

questions.explanation: The smallest molecules have the lowest boiling points and remain as gases longest, rising to the top of the column where it is coolest. Larger molecules condense lower down.

questions.stem: As the chain length of hydrocarbons increases, what happens to their viscosity (thickness)?
questions.explanation: Longer hydrocarbon chains have stronger intermolecular forces, making them more viscous (thicker and less runny). Shorter chains are thinner and flow more easily.

questions.stem: Which fraction of crude oil is used as fuel for aircraft?
questions.explanation: Kerosene (also called paraffin) is the fraction used as jet fuel for aircraft. It has the right properties of energy density, volatility, and freezing point for aviation.

questions.stem: Why is crude oil described as a finite resource?

options.text: Because it is found in only one country
Because it takes millions of years to form and is being used faster than it can be replaced

questions.explanation: Crude oil is a finite (non-renewable) resource because it takes millions of years to form from ancient organisms. We are consuming it much faster than it can be naturally replaced.

questions.stem: How does the flammability of hydrocarbon fractions change with chain length?

options.text: Flammability is the same for all chain lengths
Only the longest chains are flammable
Shorter chains are more flammable (ignite more easily)

questions.explanation: Shorter-chain hydrocarbons are more flammable and ignite more easily. This is why gases and petrol (short chains) catch fire readily, while bitumen (long chains) is difficult to ignite.
